items.title: 美國要網上直播軍法槍決胡德堡基地槍擊案兇手
items.description: 美國國防部長赫格塞斯表示，這場處決將公開進行，但一名法律專家指出，這項「前所未有」的決定處於「法律基礎不明確的領域」。
items.content:
美國要網上直播軍法槍決胡德堡基地槍擊案兇手
  - Author, 薩琳·哈貝什安（Sareen Habeshian）
- Published
- 閱讀時間: 4 分鐘
美國國防部長皮特·赫格塞思（Pete Hegseth）表示，公眾將能夠觀看一名前美國陸軍少校以行刑隊槍決方式被處決。
美國國防部一名官員向BBC表示，2009年在胡德堡（Fort Hood）槍殺13名手無寸鐵美軍士兵的納達爾·馬里克·哈桑（Nidal Hasan）將被直播處決。
外界認為，這將是美國近一個世紀以來首次公開處決。長期代表死刑犯的律師約翰·米爾斯（John Mills）表示，決定直播處決在「現代時代前所未有」，而且處於「法律基礎不明確的領域」。
赫格塞思表示：「我們會確保民眾能夠觀看，確保它是公開的。」
「人們需要明白，這類事情會帶來嚴重後果。」
五角大樓本星期稍早宣布將處決哈桑，這將是60多年來首次軍事處決。
赫格塞思在接受保守派電視台「真美國之聲」（Real America's Voice）訪問時稱，哈桑「將面對由士兵組成的行刑隊槍決，本應如此」。
當被問及哈桑是否提出任何最後要求，或曾聯絡總統唐納德·特朗普（Donald Trump；川普）時，赫格塞思表示：「不在乎。12月3日見分曉。」
五角大樓發言人肖恩·帕內爾（Sean Parnell）星期一（10月5日）表示，國防部長已提出建議，而特朗普已批准。
BBC已聯絡白宮，詢問特朗普是否支持直播公開處決。
去年全球17個國家共執行超過2700次處決，但只有兩個國家公開執行處決。
根據國際特赦組織（Amnesty International）資料，伊朗於2025年已知共執行11次公開處決，阿富汗則有六次。
美國陸軍部長星期二（6日）表示，處決定於12月3日在得州胡德堡舉行。這將是自第二次世界大戰結束以來首次以行刑隊方式執行的軍事處決。
來自弗吉尼亞州（Virginia；維珍尼亞州）的美國陸軍精神科醫生哈桑承認，他就是這宗美國軍事基地史上最致命非戰鬥襲擊事件中的槍手。
2009年11月5日的槍擊案發生在一座擠滿人的醫療大樓內，當時即將部署的士兵正在等待體檢及接種疫苗。
哈桑在法庭上曾就「任何錯誤」道歉。他在2013年的軍事法庭審訊中表示，自己相信是在保護穆斯林及阿富汗的塔利班。
根據軍法，執行軍事處決須獲美國總統批准。此外還須經過上訴覆核程序，即由上級法院審查裁決，並就其合法性作出最終判決後方可執行。
米爾斯表示，哈桑的上訴程序尚未結束，他很可能會向聯邦法院尋求覆核其定罪和刑罰，而這很可能會暫緩執行處決。
因此，米爾斯表示，如果處決真的進行，他會感到意外。
他補充說：「試圖把它變成直播的行刑隊處決，無非是特朗普政府博取關注之舉，而且不太可能真的發生，更遑論帶來任何近似司法公義的結果。」
耶魯大學法學院（Yale Law School）客座講師尤金·R·菲德爾（Eugene R Fidell）告訴BBC，這是一項「非常不幸的決定」。
他說：「直播處決簡直像是回到中世紀。作為一個社會，我們本應早已超越這種做法，至少今天之前我是這麼認為的。」
菲德爾表示，如果哈桑採取法律行動，「相關程序將持續多年」，而且「遠遠超過特朗普在白宮的任期」。
部分州份要求以某種形式公開觀看處決。許多州要求記者在場，而即將被處決的人亦可邀請他人出席。另一些州則允許普通民眾自願成為見證人。
但研究美國處決方式的紐約福坦莫大學（Fordham University；福德姆大學）法律教授黛博拉·丹諾（Prof Deborah Denno）指出：「（美國）從來沒有直播過處決。」
她表示，直播處決將「帶來一種我們國家可能前所未見的透明度」。
她說：「全國超過一半民眾支持死刑，儘管這個比例正在下降。可以提出一個論點：『如果你支持死刑，那麼我們就讓你看看這個國家如何執行死刑。』人們將不得不真正意識到究竟發生了什麼，而不是像很多人那樣選擇忽視。」
丹諾表示，直播還涉及重要考量，例如是否設有年齡限制，以及是否違反承載直播的平台政策。
目前尚不清楚直播將在哪裡提供。大多數主要社交媒體平台均有規定，禁止或限制直播露骨內容。
Meta、YouTube、TikTok和X等最知名且使用最廣泛、具備直播功能的網絡平台，不僅禁止暴力圖片和影片，也禁止展示死亡內容。
Instagram、Facebook及Threads母公司Meta明確禁止任何死刑執行直播。
TikTok亦有類似的全面禁令。其政策寫道：「我們不允許極度血腥、暴力或令人不安的內容，特別是可能對觀眾造成情緒困擾的內容。」
X平台在埃隆·馬斯克（Elon Musk）接管後已放寬內容審核政策。其政策指出，展示人物死亡時刻的內容，如接獲死者家屬或授權代表要求，將被移除。
BBC已聯絡上述公司尋求回應。
特朗普擁有的社交媒體平台「真相社交」（TRUTH Social）目前並不提供用戶直播影片功能。
國際特赦組織資料顯示，去年執行處決次數最多的國家依次為中國、伊朗、沙特阿拉伯、也門及美國。
雖然特朗普從未公開主張公開處決，但他長期支持死刑。例如1989年，他曾在《紐約時報》（The New York Times）刊登大幅廣告，要求處決被稱為「中央公園五人組」（Central Park Five）的人士。這些人當時被裁定強姦及襲擊罪成，但後來獲平反。
特朗普過去曾譴責伊朗的公開處決，並曾以伊朗政府可能殺害示威者作為理由之一，主張在今年稍早對該國發動軍事行動。
美國聯邦政府曾有17年未執行任何死刑，直到特朗普首個總統任期的最後一年，聯邦政府密集執行了13宗處決。
去年1月重返白宮後，特朗普迅速推翻前任總統喬·拜登（Joe Biden）對聯邦處決的暫停令，並簽署行政命令，旨在「恢復」死刑及「保障公共安全」。
美國上一次軍事處決發生於1961年，當時一名美國陸軍二等兵因強姦一名11歲奧地利女童罪成而被絞刑處死。該處決獲時任總統德懷特·艾森豪威爾（Dwight D Eisenhower）批准，並在受害人家屬向其繼任者約翰·肯尼迪（John F Kennedy；甘迺迪）請求赦免後仍照常執行。
美國上一次以行刑隊方式執行軍事處決是在1945年1月。當時，年輕的美國陸軍逃兵艾迪·斯洛維克（Eddie Slovik）於第二次世界大戰最後數月遭槍決。
補充報導：夸西·賈姆菲·阿西杜（Kwasi Gyamfi Asiedu）、卡莉·海斯（Kali Hays）

items.title: 老撾的班根軍用機場 中國能用來做甚麼？
items.description: 專家認為，未來的班根軍事設施可能承擔更多功能，而不僅僅是一個普通的訓練中心。
items.content:
老撾的班根軍用機場 中國能用來做甚麼？
  - Author, BBC越南語（BBC News Vietnamese）
- Published
- 閱讀時間: 6 分鐘
2026年10月8日，越南總理黎明興正式訪問老撾（寮國），並在首都萬象（永珍）與該國領導人會晤。
這次出訪受到越南國內輿論關注，因為這是黎明興以政府領導人身分進行的首次雙邊訪問。而他也是老撾新任總理沙倫賽（Saleumxay Kommasith）接待的首位外國領導人。
但對國際觀察人士而言，關注焦點落在距離萬象以北50多公里的班根（Ban Keun；賓昆），當地由中國與老撾合作建設的航空軍事設施已投入運作一個多星期。
該設施包括中老聯合保障和訓練中心，以及中老友誼航空學院。
外界關注度進一步升高，因為路透社10月6日一篇分析最新衛星影像的報導顯示，機場內出現約八架K-8教練兼輕型攻擊機，以及20多輛支援車輛。
K-8是一款由中國與巴基斯坦合作研發的雙座噴射教練機，主要用於培訓軍事飛行員，必要時亦可執行部分輕型作戰任務。
這是發展中國家較為廣泛使用的教練機型之一，並已出口至世界多國空軍。根據總部設於倫敦的國際戰略研究所（IISS）數據，老撾空軍目前擁有四架K-8。
在班根的建設工程仍持續加速推進之際，國防及外交專家正密切關注該設施未來是否會增添更多基礎設施與新能力。
因為無論該設施出現任何變化，都將為鄰國帶來一定程度的憂慮，尤其是越南。
從西南方向來看，中國已可接觸柬埔寨的雲壤（Ream）海軍基地；而在西面，班根設施則可能為北京建立在老撾的常駐軍事存在創造條件。在東面，中國也已在南中國海建設並軍事化多個設施。
因此，一旦與中國爆發危機或衝突，越南將處於不少觀察人士所稱的「四面受敵」局面。
正因如此，黎明興總理於9月中旬在國防學院發表講話時表示，越南必須為應對前所未有的軍事與國防情況做好準備。
BBC越南語（BBC News Vietnamese）已聯絡中國國防部及中國外交部，就此事尋求評論。
中國可能如何發展老撾的設施？
路透社取得的班根設施最新衛星影像顯示，目前已有一條約2000米長跑道、一條滑行道、數萬平方米停機坪及一座空中交通管制塔。大部分支援基礎設施已經完成。
該機場建於名為 Lima Site 44 的簡易機場舊址之上。該機場曾是越戰時期跑道網絡的一部分，當年美軍及美國中央情報局（CIA）曾利用這些設施，秘密支援苗族反共武裝力量。
然而，衛星影像顯示，新機場規模遠大於戰時修建的狹窄紅土跑道。
班根的位置也被認為具交通優勢，靠近中老鐵路走廊，有助更容易地將人員、裝備及物資從中國運往老撾。
分析人士認為該地點在首都萬象附近，有利於培訓工作，也方便老撾政府管理及協調設施運作。
周邊地勢相對平坦，有別於老撾大部分山地地形，更適合修建機場及開展飛行訓練項目。
東南亞大陸部分重要城市，例如越南河內和泰國曼谷，均位於班根方圓約500至700公里範圍內。即使距離較遠的地點，也僅在1000多公里之外。
新加坡南洋理工大學拉惹勒南國際研究院安全專家許瑞麟博士（Dr Collin Koh）對BBC越南語說：「目前而言，把該設施視為一個訓練中心較為恰當。」
「然而，這類設施往往也是一個方便的起點與掩護，未來可能承擔更多功能，而不僅僅是培訓用途。」
中國軍事評論人士在接受中國—全球南方計劃（CGSP）訪問時亦認為，該設施的潛力遠不止於飛行員訓練。
中國—全球南方計劃引述中國知名軍事評論博客「軍武次位面」稱，班根設施的建立，已為老撾空軍未來全面轉向採用中國製裝備「鋪平道路」。
中國國防部網站發布的公告表示，該設施由雙方共同維護及運營，旨在協助老撾加強空軍飛行員培訓，並強調「不針對任何第三方」。
然而，公告並未提供關於駐軍人數及裝備數量的更多資訊。
許瑞麟博士認為，班根設施可能作為中國空軍的後勤基地，執行已公開宣佈的支援功能。此外，當中國部隊前往泰國參加演習時，該地也可能成為方便的中途停靠點。
許瑞麟博士強調，該設施顯然標誌著中國在東南亞建立長期軍事存在的開端，尤其是在此前已存在相關安排的背景下，例如允許中國海軍進入柬埔寨雲壤海軍基地的協議。
持相似觀點的美國地緣政治預測公司 Anadyr Horizon 行政總裁阿維德·貝爾博士（Dr Arvid Bell）向BBC表示，現在下結論仍為時尚早，班根的長遠重要性將取決於該設施如何發展，以及中國未來數年如何使用它。
貝爾指出，班根不會令中國軍事能力突然大幅提升，但確實為北京未來提供更多戰略選項。
「該設施也可能為中國帶來顯著戰略利益，包括更經常的進入權限、與老撾軍方建立更深層次的制度聯繫，以及未來可進一步擴展的基礎設施。」
軍武次位面公眾號亦持相同看法，認為在班根建立支援基地，將有助中國未來「影響中南半島」。
越南「有充分理由感到憂慮」
觀察人士指出，在中國於柬埔寨及南海的存在持續增加背景下，北京對越南周邊戰略接近通道的影響力正在增強，因此越南對班根設施「有充分理由感到憂慮」。
許瑞麟博士對BBC說：「我認為，越南一直密切關注這些發展，從柬埔寨的雲壤海軍基地及德崇扶南運河項目，到中國在南海大規模增強軍事存在，再到如今老撾的班根。」
許瑞麟博士認為，若班根作為情報、監視、偵察及後勤支援基地，將成為中國人民解放軍的一項有價值補充，但他同時指出其優勢亦存在局限。
「若班根要真正對南海產生戰略影響，中國軍方必須能夠獲得介於老撾與南海之間東南亞國家的領空通行及使用權。」
泰國未必會如外界想像般願意合作，因其仍需考慮與美國的同盟義務。
越南幾乎肯定不會給予中國軍機通行權或允許其飛越本國領空，尤其是在越南本身涉及衝突的情況下。
一旦爆發重大衝突，如果中國計劃於戰時利用班根執行任務，老撾甚至可能被捲入戰爭。
許瑞麟博士認為，萬象非常清楚自身在冷戰時期的沉痛歷史教訓，當時老撾曾成為大國對抗的代理戰場。
他總結道：「班根對中國而言，很可能更多具有政治與象徵意義，而非真正具備重大作戰價值。」
老撾與越南之間擁有深厚的歷史及國防關係，同時在經濟上亦與中國日益緊密。
貝爾向BBC表示：「這兩種關係完全可以並存。」
他認為需要觀察的是，中國在軍事領域日益加深的介入，是否會改變各方影響力平衡，尤其是在安全領域，而越南長期以來一直在此扮演異常重要的角色。
另一方面，澳洲戰略政策研究所（Australian Strategic Policy Institute, ASPI）高級研究員尤安·格雷厄姆（Euan Graham）向德國之聲（DW）表示，越南長期將老撾及柬埔寨視為西側的重要戰略緩衝區。數十年來，河內一直努力維持對兩國的重要政治及軍事影響力。
談到班根時，格雷厄姆指出，河內正面臨一種令人擔憂的可能性，即在戰略上遭中國包圍。
「老撾的新空軍基地肯定會令越南的防務規劃與部署工作更加複雜。」
在新加坡國立尤索夫伊薩東南亞研究所（ISEAS-Yusof Ishak Institute）2026年的一項調查中，越南民眾對中國政治及戰略影響力增長的憂慮程度為東南亞最高，比例高達88.7%。
班根有哪些值得關注之處？
許瑞麟博士表示：「從北京一貫的做法來看，這一進程（發展成軍事基地）很可能是循序漸進且長期進行的。因此，除非出現『黑天鵝』事件（即極少發生但影響巨大的事件），否則我們大概不會看到現有設施突然升級為完整的軍事基地。」
不過，他指出，若把班根放在中國與老撾整體軍事合作框架下觀察，可以預見該設施首先會成為兩國聯合訓練及演習的集結地點。
這將為中國的軍事存在在班根逐步常態化鋪路，同時降低區域國家的疑慮。
其後，中國人民解放軍空軍在當地的存在可能逐步增加。
如果老撾空軍繼續向中國採購更先進裝備，以取代現有大部分老舊機隊，這種情況將更有可能出現。屆時，解放軍空軍與老撾空軍的訓練合作範圍與程度可能進一步擴大，並帶動更多中國先進飛機及裝備部署至班根。
許瑞麟博士亦以雲壤作例子。
過去數年，北京曾派遣兩艘解放軍海軍056型護衛艦到雲壤訓練柬埔寨部隊，為該國接收中國建造的同型新軍艦作準備。
這種模式可能成為解放軍空軍以訓練名義在班根維持半常駐存在的「藍圖」。
Anadyr Horizon 的貝爾博士認為，如果出現輪換部署解放軍人員、增加軍用運輸機航班頻率，或擴充燃料儲存設施等情況，那將是北京正朝建立班根長期後勤存在方向發展的跡象。
已公布協議是否顯示中國獲得某些使用該設施的特殊權利，同樣值得關注。
至於建造加固機堡，或經常部署中國戰鬥機、無人機和偵察機，若真的出現，則將顯示該設施正逐漸由訓練功能轉變為作戰軍事基地。
貝爾說：「如果另一個東南亞國家也採用類似的『聯合支援與訓練中心』模式，將強化外界對中國正在區內建立更廣泛軍事存在網絡的看法。」
貝爾表示，如果這類跡象也出現在區內其他地點，將更有力地證明班根屬於北京建立軍事存在網絡大戰略的一部分，而非單純的一項雙邊合作項目。
他亦提醒應保持審慎，不應賦予班根尚未獲證實的能力。其戰略價值未必在於中國眼下能夠做什麼，而在於它能協助北京降低未來擴張存在或部署更大能力所需的時間與成本。
基地鄰近萬象且接近泰國邊境，也令其位置具有一定戰略意義。
「不過，任何從班根延伸出的軍事力量投射能力，都必須與中國原本已能從雲南省實現的能力相比較評估。」
對北京的依賴
老撾是一個由老撾人民革命黨領導的一黨制低收入國家，並與兩個共產主義鄰國——中國及越南——保持長期而複雜的關係。
老撾空軍規模不大，只運作少量中國及俄羅斯製造的飛機。
在許多人看來，若考慮到過去約20年間中國在老撾影響力迅速擴張，班根的發展並不令人意外。
老撾愈來愈依賴中國的投資與資金來源。批評者經常指責北京推行「債務陷阱」外交。
在「一帶一路」倡議框架下，中國向老撾提供了價值數十億美元貸款，用於發展能源基礎設施及高速鐵路，希望推動長期經濟增長。
湄公河上的水電大壩及其他由中國資助的能源項目，被寄望把老撾打造為「東南亞電池」。
據國際貨幣基金組織（IMF）數據，老撾去年公共債務約相當於國內生產總值（GDP）的81%，而中國是其最大的雙邊債權國。
今年6月，老撾國家主席通倫（Thongloun Sisoulith）訪問北京，會晤中國國家主席習近平。習近平當時呼籲兩國建立涵蓋國防等多個領域的戰略對話機制。
一名不具名的東南亞外交官向路透社表示，過去老撾軍人通常需要前往越南、俄羅斯或中國接受高級培訓，如今部分培訓活動可能在國內即可進行。
該人士亦認為，中國正在擴大其在整個區域的軍事存在，並以中國與印尼合作建設彈藥工廠為例。
更大的問題在於，正如阿爾維德·貝爾所言，東南亞是否能夠防止大國競爭日益激烈，演變成如同歐洲及中東目前所面對的長期緊張局勢。
若要做到這一點，區域需要更多透明度、建立信任措施，以及足夠有效的合作機制，以便在各國安全決策引發更廣泛連鎖反應之前管理不穩定因素。
關於班根的人員、裝備及相關進入安排若能提供更清晰資訊，將有助鄰國更準確評估該設施的真正角色。
貝爾表示：「班根是一項考驗，用來觀察東南亞國家能否在大國軍事競爭日益加劇的情況下，同時維持區域合作與自身戰略自主。」

items.title: 台灣AV盛極而衰：中國市場如何催生這場成人片熱潮？
items.description: 台灣曾被視為亞洲唯一能合法拍攝無碼成人影片的地區，並在2020年前後快速擴張。隨著片商「麻豆傳媒」停運，外界開始質疑這波繁榮是否與中國市場及博弈資金有關。
items.content:
台灣AV盛極而衰：中國市場如何催生這場成人片熱潮？
台灣AV盛極而衰：中國市場如何催生這場成人片熱潮？
  - Author, 李洛
  - Role, BBC中文記者
  - Reporting from, 台北
- Published
台灣被視為「亞洲唯一能合法拍攝無碼成人影片」的地區，並曾在2020年前後迎來產業快速擴張。
有AV演員向BBC中文表示，高峰時期全台片商超過20家，每月產出180至300支作品。學者估計，相關成人娛樂產業產值可達新台幣200億元。
然而，隨著大型片商「麻豆傳媒」於2026年突然停運，台灣成人影片產業的興衰再度受到關注。
多名從業者透露，產業在疫情期間快速成長，背後可能與中國市場需求、線上博弈廣告及灰色資金流入有關。近年隨著資金退潮及龍頭企業倒下，整個產業正面臨巨大挑戰。
BBC中文採訪多位AV女優、導演、製作公司員工及學者，探討台灣成人影片產業如何崛起、如何轉型，以及在缺乏明確監管下面對什麼亂象。

items.title: 扎克伯格有形象問題，為何Meta的業務卻蒸蒸日上？
items.description: 一部新電影將扎克伯格的描繪成一個反派角色。但這家科技公司的收益及產品似乎不受負面形象的影響。
items.content:
扎克伯格的形象岌岌可危，但Meta的業務卻蒸蒸日上
  - Author, 莉莉·賈馬利（Lily Jamali）
  - Role, BBC北美科技記者
- Published
- 閱讀時間: 5 分鐘
上個月，在公司一年一度的 Meta Connect 產品大會上，該公司主事者馬克·扎克伯格（Mark Zuckerberg；祖克柏）發表主題演講僅過三分鐘，他的語調就變得近乎傷感。
「建造是一種愛的行為，」他雙手插兜，低頭看著地面說道：「這是我們傳遞信仰的方式，我們將自己的心血和靈魂傾注到我們所創造的東西中。」
在與數百名分析師和開發者交流時，扎克伯格還繼續分享了 Meta 最新人工智慧產品的消息：其嶄新智慧聊天機器人 Muse、一系列智慧眼鏡，以及用戶可以戴在手腕上的類似電子寵物的人工智能（artificial intelligence, AI；人工智慧）小工具。
這是一場以新技術為主題的會議，但值得注意的是，在近一個小時的演講中，扎克伯格並沒有提到他最受歡迎的兩款產品：Instagram 和臉書（Facebook）：這兩個社交媒體平台幫助 Meta 成為一家市值2萬億美元（13.4萬億元人民幣；63.8兆元新台幣）的公司。
在過去一年的大部分時間裡，Meta 一直深陷於一系列法律訴訟之中，被指控故意設計會讓年輕用戶上癮的產品。
這導致內部電子郵件、公司文件和舉報人證詞被公開，全國各地的個人傷害律師和檢察官都利用這些資料來支持他們的案件。
而且，扎克伯格這個人物並不受歡迎。去年，皮尤研究中心（Pew Research Center）的一項民調發現，三分之二的美國人對他持負面看法。
本週上映的艾倫·索金（Aaron Sorkin）執導的電影《社會清算》（The Social Reckoning ；《社群清算》）恐怕難以挽回他的聲譽。
這部電影講述的是舉報人聲稱 Meta 公司高層其實知道其產品會傷害年輕人。
根據《好萊塢報道》（Hollywood Reporter）的一篇影評稱，《繼承之戰》（Succession）演員傑瑞米·斯特朗（Jeremy Strong；傑瑞米·史壯／謝洛美·史壯）在片中飾演扎克伯格，將他塑造成一個「徹頭徹尾的反派」，電影中他「泰然自若地主張，一旦涉及金錢，就算表現出最微小的責任感也是大忌」。
有人猜測，這是 Meta 的「煙草巨頭時刻」。因為公眾逐漸形成反對該公司以及整個社交媒體行業的共識。
但，事實似乎更為複雜。
因為，儘管數月來負面新聞不斷，但 Meta 的產品在現實世界中卻表現得比以往任何時候都好。其應用程式的使用量持續成長，用戶也紛紛湧向其全新的AI人工智慧助理。
這就引出了一個問題：究竟有什麼能真正限制 Meta 的發展？或者它現在已經成為一家「不沾鍋」公司，醜聞對它來說根本無關緊要？
Meta 的「信任赤字」
對 Meta 來說，這無疑是負面新聞不斷的一年。
去年夏天，路透社便披露 Meta 允許其聊天機器人「與兒童進行浪漫或色情對話」，並向用戶提供虛假醫療資訊。
Meta 已修改了這些政策，並表示根本不應該允許此類回應。
今年，帳單更是接踵而至。
3月，陪審團裁定，一名20歲的加州女子因使用Meta旗下的Instagram和谷歌旗下的YouTube而遭受精神健康損害，並判給她600萬美元（4,020萬元人民幣；1.92億元新台幣）的賠償。
大約在同一時間，新墨西哥州成為第一個在針對 Meta 的兒童安全訴訟中勝訴的州份。陪審團認定該公司未能就其平台對兒童構成的危險向公眾發出警告。
Meta 被處以總計9.42億美元的罰款。法官稱 Meta 是「公害」，如同空氣污染。
不過，Meta 公司表示不同意判決結果，將對兩起案件提起上訴。
今年5月，Meta 與其他幾家社交公司一起，透過與肯塔基州某學區達成和解，避免了審判。
該學區指控 Meta 的產品設計導致了一起青少年心理健康危機。據報道，Meta 同意支付900萬美元和解，是所有被告中金額最高的。
此外，今年夏天，Meta 與美國48個州、哥倫比亞特區以及三個美國屬地達成了一項備受矚目的180億美元和解協議。 Meta 在和解協議中否認有不當行為，並在為期五天的庭審中堅稱多年來，公司投入大量資源進行測試和研究，致力於提昇平台對年輕用戶的安全性。
作為協議的一部分，Meta承諾對年輕用戶實施每日兩小時的使用時長限制，並設定夜間使用限制、在校期間靜音通知等措施。
該公司還面臨其他訴訟，包括本月稍後在洛杉磯開庭的訴訟，該訴訟也與年輕用戶涉嫌社群媒體成癮有關。
同時，包括澳洲在內的多個國家已開始全面禁止兒童使用社群媒體。澳洲於去年12月率先實施了這項禁令。
儘管社群媒體公司的產品仍然很受歡迎，但這些公司普遍不受歡迎。根據路透社—益普索（Reuters/Ipsos）的一項調查，85%的美國人認為社群媒體會讓兒童上癮，61%的人支持政府加強監管。
對某些人來說，信任問題關乎生死存亡。
「一旦大眾不再信任你，就會陷入惡性循環，」紐約大學史特恩商學院副教授泰勒（Alison Taylor）強調。
「感覺⋯⋯信任危機太嚴重了，我不知道他們是否還能恢復。」
「頂住反彈」
儘管發生了這些備受矚目的案件，但該公司報告稱，其部分應用程式（如 Instagram 和 WhatsApp）的用戶數量同比增長了3%，今年第二季度的收入比2025年同期增長了28%。
雖然 Meta 已同意放緩對青少年市場的投資（許多品牌都熱衷於開拓青少年市場以建立未來的用戶群），但該公司表示，青少年用戶在其收入中所佔比例不到1%。
其競爭對手 TikTok 和谷歌（Google）旗下的 YouTube 更受年輕用戶歡迎。
該公司與美國48州達成的和解協議被普遍認為是 Meta 公司的重大勝利，因為它避免了部分 Meta 高層（包括扎克伯格）出庭作證，並阻止了更多內部文件的公開，同時也讓公司避免了承認不當行為。
這個消息公佈後，公司股價立即上漲4%，過去一個月累計漲幅超過25%。
批評人士中一種流行的觀點是，該公司試探了消費者對不良行為的容忍度，而迄今為止，其業務大多成功經受住了這種負面影響。
換言之，即使人們不喜歡這家公司，他們也會繼續使用其產品。
「我認為他們目前的處境非常好，這出乎我的意料，」科技顧問公司穆爾洞見與策略（Moor Insights & Strategy）的創始人兼總裁帕特里克·穆爾黑德（Patrick Moorhead）說。
Meta 的新型 AI 代理
然而，Meta 進軍人工智能領域在一定程度上取決於重建公眾信任。
上個月，該公司推出了新的人工智能個人助理應用程式 Muse。
至關重要的是，Muse 是一個人工智慧代理，這意味著它可以分多個階段執行任務，並持續工作數小時（這與 ChatGPT 等聊天機器人不同，後者往往一次只能執行一項任務）。
這是首款由大型科技公司推出並公開發布的AI智慧助理。
一位《紐約時報》科技記者試用了這款應用程式兩週後表示，「驚嘆不已。因為這款應用程式可以代表他聯繫牙科保險公司，幫他訂購食品雜貨，並在電子表格中記錄他的信用卡消費。
但是，當用戶將一些最私人的資訊交給該公司時，Muse 才能發揮最佳效果，譬如信用卡資訊、購買歷史記錄和電子郵件收件匣的存取權限。
對於一家隱私聲譽早已受損的公司來說，這是一個很高的要求。
差不多十年前，劍橋分析公司（Cambridge Analytica）醜聞曝光，數百萬 Facebook 用戶的資料遭到洩露，並被一家政治顧問公司利用，該公司的隱私聲譽因此蒙上陰影。
就在扎克伯格在 Meta Connect 大會上發表主題演講兩天后，新墨西哥州的另一個陪審團裁定 Meta 在 Facebook 如何使用個人資訊的問題上撒謊。（不過，該公司表示不同意這項裁決，並將為自己辯護，反駁其所謂的歪曲事實的行為。）
那麼，使用者是否願意為了方便使用 Muse 而交出這些資料呢？
一些用戶表示贊同。
Muse 自一個月前上線以來，下載量已超過500萬次，週活躍用戶超過300萬——在北美市場，其普及速度超過了 ChatGPT 最初推出時的水平。
扎克伯格描繪了一幅願景：Muse 將與不斷擴展的 Meta AI 智慧眼鏡系列相結合，使用戶能夠免提召喚他所謂的「個人超級智慧」。
Meta 顯然對其智慧眼鏡寄予厚望。
「我認為他們正在投資，力圖將自己打造為品類領導者，」弗雷斯特市場咨詢（Forrester）負責社交媒體和網紅領域的首席分析師凱特·威尼克（Kate Winick）表示。
他又強調：「無論這個品類最終發展到多大規模，他們目前都將佔據主導地位。」
這款眼鏡引發了爭議，有些人甚至稱之為「變態眼鏡」，因為它可以用來秘密拍攝。
該公司已採取措施，阻止用戶篡改用於指示正在拍攝照片或影片的指示燈。
扎克伯格也剛發布了新款純音訊智慧眼鏡，這顯然是為了平息人們對隱私的擔憂。
但，該公司最激烈的批評者仍保持謹慎。
倡議組織「熱倡議」（Heat Initiative）的布魯克·伊斯圖克（Brooke Istook）批評：「消費者都知道 Meta 公司存在問題，而且到目前為止我們一直無法信任他們能夠生產出對兒童安全的商品。那麼，消費者為什麼要把一些最私密、最敏感的信息託付給他們呢？」
隱私權與便利
扎克伯格在演講中簡單提及了隱私這一敏感議題。
演講期間，他身後的螢幕上閃過一幅畫面：迪士尼的吉祥物 Muse 抱著一把藍色的鎖。
扎克伯格告訴觀眾：「考慮到 Muse 和眼鏡上的內容都非常私密，我們從一開始就將最先進的隱私和安全設計融入到所有這些系統中。」
例如，他大力推廣個人虛擬機器——本質上是一個運行在 Meta 雲端的獨立電腦系統，據稱 Muse 用戶的資料將儲存在其中。
對此，扎克伯格承諾將確保每位用戶的資訊安全，並表示不久後「即使是 Meta 也無法查看這些資訊」。
他還表示該虛擬機器將於今年稍後推出，並將推出更多隱私保護措施。
Meta 對隱私和安全的重視似乎旨在讓消費者安心。
但，分析師威尼克表示，用戶仍需要選擇啟用許多此類保護措施。 她說：「我認為如果他們覺得可以不啟用這些措施，他們就會這麼做」。
扎克伯格在加州發表演說後不久，社群媒體用戶就開始舉報 Muse 失控的案例，包括該助理未經許可讀取電子郵件。
Meta 公司否認了這些指控，並表示他們不認為 Muse 會在未經用戶同意的情況下存取電子郵件。
分析師穆爾黑德則向BBC指出，最終，如果能換來便利性和實用性，大多數用戶或許願意在隱私方面做出一些讓步。
他說：「如果消費者認為這種權衡是有利的，他們就會繼續下去，這就是為什麼 Facebook 和 Instagram 至今仍擁有數十億用戶的原因。」
此外，在財務方面，社群媒體廣告業務——其搖錢樹——通常能帶來可觀的收入。
Meta 公佈今年第二季營收為608億美元，獲利159億美元。
持續的利潤推動了從備受嘲諷的元宇宙到目前人工智慧基礎設施的大規模擴張等一系列投資。
那麼在 Muse 上呢？
威尼克向BBC分析：「這是一個非常實際的節省時間的好處，很多人都會想要並且喜歡它。」
但，人工智慧投資成本不菲。
根據Meta公司最新的財務報表，其長期債務已高達837億美元。
儘管如此，Meta 的高層對公司向人工智慧的轉型充滿信心。
該公司首席技術官安德魯·博斯沃思（Andrew Bosworth）接受BBC採訪時解釋：「這實際上關乎你的代理人，他可以代表你工作，在你實現人生目標的過程中，他始終是你可靠的盟友。」
Meta 雄心勃勃，但它的未來最終可能取決於用戶是否信任它。

items.title: 法國學生示威：憤怒背後隱藏著什麼？
items.description: 法國中學生示威來自對制度的不滿，但也源自於法國在街頭與制定政策的傳統。
items.content:
法國學生示威：憤怒背後隱藏著什麼？
  - Author, 亨利·阿斯蒂爾 （Henri Astier）
- Published
- 閱讀時間: 3 分鐘
自9月下旬以來，法國各地的學生一直在舉行抗議活動，反對教育經費不足，並封鎖了許多高中校園入口。
這場運動在一些地方演變成暴力事件——數百名學生、教師和警察受傷，數千人被捕，其中包括數量不明的外部滋事分子。
抗議者抱怨該國高中——15至18歲學生就讀的學校——師資短缺和設施破舊。
巴黎學生瑪達萊娜（Madalena）週二（10月6日）告訴BBC：「有時候我們的老師會缺席好幾個星期，而且沒有替補老師，」。
在當天，法國各地爆發了數十萬人參與的示威遊行。這名學生補充說，在最近的熱浪期間，學校的教學大樓裡「熱得像蒸籠一樣」。
還有其他各種各樣的抱怨。
有些人不滿學校禁止使用手機，或放學時間縮短到18:00。
「19:00才能到家，根本沒時間睡覺或做作業，」一位高中生告訴法國電視第二台（France 2）。
法國負責分配高等教育名額的線上平台 「Parcoursup」（編按：類似台灣大學入學分發系統或香港JUPAS），是另一個痛點。
學生對此不滿由來已久。
如今每個年級約有80%學生能通過法國業士文憑（baccalauréat；法國高考），因而取得大學入學資格——但不一定是他們心儀的科系。這導致學生爭搶熱門課程，焦慮也集中在許多人視為不透明的入學系統 Parcoursup 上。
這些不滿是真實存在的。但它們本身就能解釋抗議運動所採取的形式嗎？法國與其他國家相比如何？
根據已開發國傢俱樂部經合組織最近的報告，法國政府在高中生人均教育支出高於歐盟高中平均。
教師短缺問題確實十分嚴峻，但並不比其他地方更嚴重。
以經濟合作與發展組織（OECD）的標準來看，法國的情況實際上更為溫和——空缺職位較少——儘管法國教師的薪水相對較低。
對法國學生來說，上課時間拖到下午很晚確實是個問題。這主要是因為午休時間過長和課程安排複雜，而不是因為假期太長——與其他歐盟國家相比，法國的假期並不算長。
延長上課時間一直是法國學校生活中一個令人遺憾的現象，因此很難解釋當前的爆發。
此外，高等教育體系功能失調所帶來的壓力也無法解釋這波示威潮。
因為，在大多數歐洲國家，80%至90%的年輕人會完成中學教育，而爭奪好的大學名額也會在其他方面造成壓力。
雖然資金不足、建築破舊以及對未來的擔憂是學生不滿的根源，但正如內政部長洛朗·努涅斯（Laurent Nuñez）所言，這些抱怨本身並不能解釋為什麼這場運動在學校數量、學生人數以及暴力程度方面變得「史無前例」。
考慮到參與者承擔著相當大的風險，抗議活動的規模就更加引人注目了。
以威脅或武力封鎖學校或大學是違法的，會引來警察和破壞分子，學生們也常常被捲入警方的群體控制行動中，而這些行動往往手段強硬。
法國總理塞巴斯蒂安·勒科爾尼（Sébastien Lecornu）在最新演說中強調，法國安全部隊並未接到「與高中生對抗」的命令，而只是依法執法。
對此，要理解學生的策略，就必須超越學校的警戒線，探討背後的政治傳統。
因為，在法國，權力往往既掌握在民選機構手中，也掌握在街頭。
學生們深明此道。
1990年10月，塞納—聖但尼省（Seine-Saint-Denis）——巴黎北部，也是當前動盪局勢的焦點地區——一所學校發生的強暴案，引發了大規模抗議，民眾走上街頭，反對學校經費不足和師資短缺。
最終，政府撥款，以今天的幣值計算，相當於12億歐元（13.42億美元；89.97億元人民幣；429.93億元新台幣），用於資助高中教育。
1998年10月，法國50萬名學生在全國各地舉行遊行，提出類似的要求，最終爭取到近10億歐元用於翻新學校，並增聘了1.4萬名教職員工。
學生抗議曾多次挫敗政府改革——例如1986年的大學改革和1994年的降低青年最低工資。
2006年，學生力量最引人注目的一次展現，或許是他們撤回了一項旨在放寬26歲以下員工僱用和解僱規則以解決青年失業問題的法律。
該措施由議會通過，並由當時的總統雅克·希拉克（Jacques Chirac）簽署，但在大學和中學遭到數週封鎖，且經常發生暴力事件後被廢除。
法國成年人已經證明，封鎖道路可以戰勝民選官員。
2018至2019 年的「黃背心」（The Gilets Jaunes）運動——全國各地商店遭到洗劫，政府大樓遭到襲擊——迫使政府取消了燃油稅上漲計劃，並批准了100億歐元的支出。
不過，街頭法則並非總是勝利。
1968年——這項英勇的先例被每一場法國抗議運動所引用——一場學生起義最終被選舉平息。
但這些高中生繼承了一種政治文化，在這種文化中，示威者與民選官員競爭，以爭取被視為人民的合法代言人。
表面上看來目前的權力平衡對學生有利。
根據BFMTV的一項民調顯示，72%的法國人認為他們的訴求是合理的，55%的人支持這場運動。
在眾多教師、工會和左翼政治人物的支持下，抗議者佔據了主動性。
相形之下，政府從未如此弱勢。執政九年後，馬克龍（Emmanuel Macron；馬克宏）已是極不受歡迎的跛腳領袖。他依法不能參選六個月後的總統大選。
當年他在2024年6月決定提前改選，結果造就一個徹底陷入僵局的國民議會。
現在勒科爾尼自稱是「人們記憶中最弱勢的總理」，看來也很難讓預算在議會過關。
但正是這種弱勢，在總理與學生的對峙中或許反而成為資產。面對上升的借貸成本、佔國內生產毛額5.4%的赤字，以及1940年代以來最高的公共債務，勒科爾尼在財政與政治上都束手無策。
不像他的前任總理們在街頭巨大壓力下還有東西可給出去。現在的總理已沒有任何籌碼能交換示威者的讓步了。

items.title: 德语媒体：财政吃紧 北京盯上了富豪们的境外资产
items.url: https://www.dw.com/zh/德语媒体：财政吃紧-北京盯上了富豪们的境外资产/a-79618435?maca=chi-rss-chi-all-1127-rdf
items.description: 《新苏黎世报》称，经济疲软和房地产危机使中国财政收入急剧下滑，各地方政府目前都在想法设法扩展财路，富豪们的海外投资收益也成了税务追缴的重点。《经济周刊》评论称，德法联手建议欧盟采取强硬对华政策，标志着柏林已经不愿继续听从北京的摆布。
items.content:
（德国之声中文网）《新苏黎世报》发自北京的报道称，由于公共财政空虚，中国许多城镇公职人员的薪资都没法按时发放。财政困境逼迫之下，“搞钱”成了各地政府的当务之急。这篇题为《富豪成了政府追缴的猎物》的报道写道：
“当前大规模行动的针对目标，则是那些有海外投资的中国富豪。有关当局要求他们补缴拖欠的财产税。
按照相关法律规定，中国公民历来都有缴纳所谓全球所得税的义务，即在境外投资股票、债券、房地产或存款所获得的收益。不过直到前不久，投资者都可以轻易逃过纳税义务，因为中国政府部门并不知晓本国公民在海外的收益情形。
中国早在2018年就加入了所谓的‘共同申报体系’ （Common Reporting System）。在这一体系下，参与国的银行和资产管理机构会相互交换信息，包括外籍人士的账户以及收益情况等等。不过，直到最近，中国财政部门才对相关资料进行了评估，并初步掌握了本国公民拖欠税款的大致规模。香港咨询公司 Dezan Shira & Associates的Jennifer Lu写道：‘中国已经从筹备阶段进入了执行阶段。’
过去25年当中，数十万中国人跨入了富裕阶层。2001年中国的平均收入还只有1000美元，现在则已经飙升至14000美元。目前，中国已经拥有500名资产超过十亿美元的富豪。他们的部分资产被投入伦敦的房地产、美国的股市或者西方艺术品收藏。仅在香港的银行里，中国人的存款数额就已经超过了1.7万亿美元。
在政府的压力之下，过去几个月来，众多省份的税务部门不断向欠税者寄信、打电话和发送短信。据媒体报道，一些税务部门还成立了特别行动小组，专门负责搜寻亿万富豪的行踪。”
《新苏黎世报》报道称，由于当局要求在十月底之前补齐海外资产过去三到五年的拖欠税款，不安情绪正在富人群体中快速蔓延，一些人甚至试图通过更换国籍的方式来逃脱纳税义务：
“最大的问题是如何确定纳税金额。有些人收到的补税通知上罗列了明确的数额，有些人则只收到一份笼统的估算值。有关部门宣称，估算的税金可以作为双方商谈的基础。中国税务部门的操作方式似乎还没有形成固定模式，但他们收缴拖欠税款的决心显然是不容置疑的。
许多海外投资者正在想方设法补齐税款，有人借贷，有人试图将部分境外资产转回国内。但转移资金并非易事。根据中国严苛的资金流动管制，每个中国人每年只能向境外汇出五万美金，收取境外汇款也以五万为限。不过，一些省份已经发出信号，愿意放宽欠税者的汇款额度，增加财政收入的前景显然更有吸引力。
根据巴克莱银行对所谓‘极端场景’的推算，仅香港一地的中国投资者财产，就可以给中国带来大约一千亿的税务收入。不过，即便在世界其他地区的海外投资也能为中国公共财政带来类似规模的税务收入，恐怕仍难以填补巨大的财政缺口。中国的债务总额已超过国内生产总值的300%以上。 ”
"德国绝不可以继续天真了"
德国总理默茨和法国总统马克龙共同建议，在贸易冲突严重升级时，欧盟应有权将相关国家彻底排除出欧盟内部市场。《经济周刊》就此写道：
“相关建议的矛头所指，政治高层可谓尽人皆知。中国出口顺差之大，已经令德国一直以来的出口顺差变成了笑料。现如今，欧洲各国都坚信，北京采用了不公平手段。中国的过剩产能正在被大量投放世界市场，各国竞争者都毫无招架之力。没有人相信，当前的状况同市场经济还有任何关联。
历来喜欢为全球化和市场经济高唱赞歌的德国总理也不例外。默茨虽然仍推崇自由主义，但他也意识到，德国绝不可以继续天真了。
新近出现的强硬及疑虑呼声，意味着对华政策出现了根本性转向。过去，每当涉及是否应对中国采取强硬立场的讨论时，德国总是会扮演刹车角色，因为德国实在是太担心遭到中国的报复了。这种担心现在也并没有消失，只是德国总理府将这种担心和凯恩斯主义进行了结合：长远来看，我们都将死去。但短期之内，我们必须勇于自卫。”

items.title: 中欧贸易投资磋商成果：混动汽车、稀土出口是看点
items.url: https://www.dw.com/zh/中欧贸易投资磋商成果：混动汽车、稀土出口是看点/a-79618304?maca=chi-rss-chi-all-1127-rdf
items.description: 10月8日和9日两天在北京举行中欧贸易投资磋商机制（简称机制）第二次例会结束后，成果共识清单公之于众。此前欧洲方面要求改善的欧中贸易逆差、中国国家补助机制等均在议题之中。
items.content:
中欧贸易投资磋商成果：混动汽车、稀土出口是看点
2026年10月9日
（德国之声中文网）中国商务部部长王文涛与欧盟委员会贸易和经济安全委员马罗什·谢夫乔维奇（Maros Sefcovic）在北京举行中欧贸易投资磋商机制（简称机制）第二次例会结束后，双方发表了会议成果共识清单。其中备受关注的包括“双方以符合世贸组织规则的方式就混动汽车贸易达成谅解。” 此外双方“将继续电动汽车反补贴案企业价格承诺复审相关程序”。在出口管制方面，中方原通过“绿色通道机制，为稀土及永磁体对欧洲出口许可审批继续提供便利。欧方将继续与成员国一道，为解决两用领域对华重点许可个案提供便利。”
此次中欧贸易投资机制例会举行的时间点并非偶然，而是欧盟对华经济安全焦虑上升，欧中贸易摩擦多点并发，以及欧盟多成员国要求欧盟对中国采取更强硬态度和措施之时。
欧中贸易逆差长居高位
欧盟对华贸易逆差长期处于高位，去年约为3600亿欧元，相当于每天近10亿欧元贸易逆差。欧洲担心中国制造业产能过剩，人民币被人为贬值创造出口优势，中国造低价产品冲击本地产业。汽车则是欧洲贸易最大的摩擦点。尤其是几十年来依靠中国市场获取巨额利润的德国汽车业倍感压力。
2024年，欧盟对中国产纯电动车征收反补贴税, 在原有10%关税之上加征, 幅度最高约35%。之后双方一直在谈"价格承诺"来替代关税, 即本次例会成果清单里提及的“继续电动汽车反补贴案企业价格承诺复审相关程序”。混动车不在欧盟关税加征范围内, 过去两年中国混动车对欧出口量增长，即清单里提及的"混动汽车贸易谅解"的背景。至于稀土等关键原材料的出口则是欧中以及美中贸易摩擦的“老话题”。欧洲指责中国以限制稀土等关键原材料出口为制衡措施，而这些原材料是欧洲工业急迫所需。此次欧中贸易投资例会在这一方面达成的相互提供审批便利的原则性一致，应被欧方认为是实质性成果。不过中国在与美国的类似谈判中也做过承诺，但美国财政部长9月份表示，中方未依照承诺，放行足够的稀土出口量。
欧盟反制中国贸易的“工具箱”
欧盟在反制对华贸易劣势的可行措施主要有反补贴征税，比如2024年实行的针对中国电动汽车的加征关税。此外还有国际采购工具(IPI)，2025年首次用于中国, 限制中国医疗器械企业参与欧盟大额（500万欧元以上）公共采购项目。取消150欧元以下小额包裹关税豁免，加强对Temu, Shein等中国廉价网购平台的监管，也是欧盟在规则市场准入方面的对策之一。
在欧盟内部，如何应对以及反制对华贸易失衡在各成员国之间并非没有分歧。德国因为支柱产业汽车业主要依靠中国市场的盈利，所以一直主张对中国采取“温和态度”。相比德国，法国的态度在反制中国、去风险化方面更为强硬。本周三（10月7日），欧洲议会以454票对86票通过了一项对华立场强硬的决议。该决议的核心诉求是“经济互惠”，并强调“若中国不开放市场，欧盟将采取相应的反制措施”。

items.description: 今年的诺贝尔和平奖授予南非女律师皮莱（Navanethem Pillay）。位于奥斯陆的诺贝尔平和委员会在周五（10月9日）宣布这一消息时表示，这是表彰她对国际法的勇敢奉献，以及为追究战争罪和种族灭绝罪做出的杰出贡献。
items.content:
南非女律师皮莱荣获2026年诺贝尔和平奖
2026年10月9日
（德国之声中文网）现年85岁的纳维·皮莱（Navanethem Pillay）出生于南非德班，父母是印度裔泰米尔人。她自20世纪60年代起在南非从事律师工作，为反种族隔离活动人士进行法律辩护，并积极参与反对酷刑的运动。1995年，她成为南非纳塔尔省高等法院首位非白人法官。
1999年至2003年，皮莱担任卢旺达问题国际刑事法庭庭长，之后在海牙国际刑事法院担任法官。2008年至2014年，她担任联合国人权事务高级专员。
在此之后，皮莱担任联合国巴勒斯坦领土问题调查委员会主席。2025年9月，她领导的委员会发布报告，指控以色列在加沙地带犯下种族灭绝罪行。以色列驳斥该报告，称其“令人愤慨”。
皮莱获得本年度诺贝尔和平奖的消息公布后，德国联邦政府向这位现年85岁的律师表示祝贺。一位政府发言人表示，皮莱“数十年来以极大的个人奉献和令人钦佩的毅力，为争取人权、正义和国际法的执行而不懈奋斗”。
人权组织国际特赦组织（Amnesty International）欢迎奥斯陆的这项决定，认为这是“在恰当的时间发出的恰当信号”。国际特赦组织德国分会秘书长杜克罗（Julia Duchrow）强调，皮莱从来直言不讳地指出罪行的本质，无论罪行是由谁犯下的，“这正是当今许多政府所缺乏的勇气。只在符合自身的政治利益时，他们才会捍卫国际法”。
南非总统西里尔·拉马福萨（Cyril Ramaphosa）也向皮莱表示祝贺，称将诺贝尔和平奖授予皮莱是对她毕生致力于正义、和平与人类尊严的致敬。
（路透社、德新社等）

items.url: https://www.dw.com/zh/公开处决！五角大楼将网上直播行刑队执行死刑/a-79615338?maca=chi-rss-chi-all-1127-rdf
items.description: 美国国防部长赫格塞斯（Pete Hegseth）本周三（10月7日）宣布，对胡德堡枪击案凶手哈桑的死刑将“公开”执行，时间定于12月3日。本周四，五角大楼确认这次执行死刑将网上现场直播，并称更多细节有待公布。
items.content:
公开处决！五角大楼将网上直播行刑队执行死刑
2026年10月9日
（德国之声中文网）五角大楼在X平台上发布的一段视频中，赫格塞斯周三表示，，对胡德堡枪击案凶手纳达尔·马利克·哈桑（Nidal Malik Hasan）执行死刑的是一支由士兵组成的行刑队，“我们要确保人们能够观看，确保它是公开的。”赫格塞斯说，“我们当然会在胡德堡举行行刑仪式”，“而且是在周四下午1点，这正是他作案的时间。
赫格塞斯是在“林肯”号航空母舰上与右翼网红波索比克（Jack Posobiec）交谈时，发表上述言论的。林肯号于周四结束了近11个月的远航任务回到加州基地 。
赫格塞斯说，“人们需要明白，枪杀这类事件会带来严重后果”。赫格塞斯还补充道，“我挺喜欢我们在二战时期的那种心态，那就是——赢得胜利。“
此前，五角大楼10月5日曾宣布，特朗普总统已根据赫格塞斯的建议批准公开处决哈桑。
五角大楼官员周四（10月8日）表示，这次枪决会对公众直播，具体细节之后会公布。
美军上一次已知的行刑队处决发生在1945年。
关于胡德堡枪击案凶手 我们了解些什么？
哈桑曾任职美国陆军精神科医生。他1970年出生在美国弗吉尼亚州，父母来自巴勒斯坦。2009年11月5日，哈桑在德克萨斯州的胡德堡陆军基地开枪射杀13人，打伤32人。美国军事法庭于2013年判处他死刑。
在审判期间，哈桑声称，他发动枪击是为了保护阿富汗塔利班成员免受美军伤害。
哈桑在被捕时遭警方枪击，导致部分瘫痪，此后一直坐轮椅。
联合国称美国直播死刑执行过程无异于“酷刑”
美国政府直播哈桑死刑执行的决定遭到了联合国人权委员会的严厉批评。该联合国机构在致法新社的一份声明中表示：“直播死刑执行过程无异于公开处决，并将违反关于绝对禁止酷刑的规定。”
该机构指出，此前针对阿富汗和伊朗的公开处决也曾发表过类似声明，称此类行为“构成一种残忍、不人道或有辱人格的待遇或惩罚”。
（法新社、美联社、路透社）

items.url: https://www.dw.com/zh/德国前情报局长涉嫌出售机密给他国-中国或扮演重要角色/a-79612102?maca=chi-rss-chi-all-1127-rdf
items.description: 德国联邦情报局(BND)前局长汉宁及其一名前下属本周因涉嫌向外国泄露机密文件被捕。《明镜周刊》周四援引消息人士独家报道称,调查人员正在核查汉宁卸任后以顾问身份与多国开展合作的情况, 其中他与中国情报部门可能的关联是调查重点之一。
items.content:
德国前情报局长涉嫌出售机密给他国 中国或扮演重要角色
2026年10月9日
（德国之声中文网）“明镜周刊”（Der Spiegel）周四（10月8日）独家报道说，现年80岁的德国情报局（BND）前任局长汉宁（August Hanning）涉嫌与中国情报部门一位男性工作人员分享了德国方面的机密信息。德国检察机关在回复“明镜周刊”的采访请求时，拒绝对上述指控表态。
尽管没有官方表态，多家德语媒体纷纷转载“明镜周刊”，报道汉宁或向中国提供情报的消息，让这一原本已经极具爆炸性的新闻获得了更多关注。
10月6日汉宁与其在任时亲信、汉宁离职后仍在联邦情报局任要职多年的曼弗雷德 D.双双被捕当天，德语媒体在报道此事时，一方面强调二人涉嫌卖国和间谍罪行，另一方面强调，据目前媒体获知的消息，涉及的出卖情报的对象国与俄罗斯无关。几家媒体在报道中提及了阿塞拜疆，并强调目前无法确认消息。
前联邦情报局汉宁被控出卖情报
汉宁于 1998‑2005 年担任联邦情报局局长，曼弗雷德 D.曾是汉宁的办公室主任。汉宁退休后，曼弗雷德继续为多位后继局长服务，直至今年年初正式退休，可谓是情报局内部最核心的知情圈成员之一。
检方指控曼弗雷德截至 2022 年 6 月已向早已退休的汉宁交付多达 2000 份标记为高度机密的内部文件, 汉宁再将这些信息出售给他国。
汉宁的辩护律师克鲁泽(Leon Kruse)周三表示, 汉宁坚决否认泄密指控。克鲁泽确认汉宁持有被列为机密的文件, 但强调他“没有在损害德国利益的情况下将这些信息转交给第三方的行为, 更没有出售信息。”
在汉宁被捕后被媒体普遍曝光的还有他退休后的收入状况。汉宁卸任情报局长后主要从事顾问咨询工作，并在多家公司担任监事会兼职，均属高层职位。此前媒体曾曝光，汉宁因曾在一家波罗的海国家银行担任监事会理事而陷入经济困境。该银行经营不善且遭受蓄意破坏，最终宣告破产。时任监事会理事的汉宁以及同为理事、前北约秘书长拉斯穆森均被牵连进银行破产程序中，需对银行及客户的损失承担责任。此事迫使原本收入丰厚、财政无忧的汉宁陷入个人财政危机，部分退休金被迫上缴以抵债。
汉宁和曼弗雷德 D.被捕的本周，德国联邦议会刚刚举行了自2016年以来每年一次的安全保护机构的公开听证会。出席听证的包括联邦情报局（BND）、联邦宪法保护局（BfV）和军事反情报局（MAD)的负责人。媒体从业人员和普通公民在提前报名的前提下，可以旁听听证会。听证会上，上述三个德国最重要情报和安全保护组织，对德国国家安全目前所处的形势给出评估，也会具体举例说明德国在哪些方面尤其受到他国的威胁。
德国安全保护机构警告来自中国的危险
今年听证会上，三个情报和安全组织负责人的评估基调围绕德国仍处在俄罗斯情报工作的攻击目标，特别是因为德国在军事和资金援助乌克兰方面扮演的重要角色。除此之外，中国也被特别提及。联邦宪法保护局警告有人利用高校交流和科研合作，获取德国专有技术，比如人工智能、量子技术和生物技术领域。此外,有关部门还注意到中国科技产品的不断扩散。从智能家电到联网汽车，用户提供的数据外流可能被滥用。在极端情况下, 甚至可能出现对系统进行远程关闭的情况。

items.title: Trump announces deal for Russian diesel as Zelensky criticises 'gift to Putin'
items.description: Ukraine's president said allowing Russia to sell petroleum products would prolong a war that must be ended.
items.content:
Trump announces deal for Russian diesel as Zelensky criticises 'gift to Putin'
- Published
US President Donald Trump says he has reached an agreement with Russian President Vladimir Putin allowing Moscow to "immediately release" diesel into the global market.
He said Putin had agreed to release 300,000 tonnes of diesel immediately, followed by 500,000 tonnes in November and another million after that.
"Diesel Prices for Americans and, indeed, the World, will be COMING DOWN, IN RECORD NUMBERS, AND FAST!" Trump wrote on Truth social.
An envoy to Putin welcomed the deal, but Ukraine's president said any easing of sanctions on Russia played into Moscow's hands and would prolong a war that must be ended.
Diesel prices in the US have doubled since the war with Iran began in February, putting pressure on Republicans ahead of the midterm elections over the rising cost of living.
The average diesel price in the US is currently $6.28 a gallon, according to the AAA, down from the record high of $6.53 recorded at the the end of September.
Shortly after Trump's announcement, the US Treasury formally issued a temporary license allowing Russian diesel into the market.
An envoy for Putin, Kirill Dmitriev, welcomed the deal on social media, saying: "Russia-US co-operation on diesel and energy will benefit the world."
But Volodymyr Zelensky hit out at the deal, saying "gifts to Putin will not work for peace" and that Russia would repay the diesel with "further terror".
"Allowing Russia to sell petroleum products is an investment in a war that must be ended, not prolonged," he wrote on social media.
This year Russia has experienced two waves of severe fuel shortages across the country as a result of Ukrainian drone strikes on Russian oil refineries.
According to the International Energy Agency, its diesel production is estimated to have fallen by nearly 30%.
Trump has expressed his displeasure over those attacks, blaming them for rising fuel prices.
But on Friday Zelensky defended the strikes, saying there were in response to "Russia's years-long campaign of terror against Ukraine's energy sector".
"Ukraine will not set Russian oil refineries on fire if Russia does not destroy our energy infrastructure," he said.
What impact the deal with Russia will have on fuel prices remains unclear. The global benchmark for crude oil, Brent, remains above $103 a barrel. Before the war with Iran, Brent crude was trading at about $73 a barrel.
The BBC has contacted the White House for comment on what reimbursement the US is providing Russia in return for the release of diesel.
It is the latest effort from the president to lower fuel prices in the US.
Earlier this week, Trump said he was "thinking about" suspending the federal tax on gasoline, and also announced that he would allow so-called red dye diesel to be used on US highways without facing federal tax.
He has also successfully pressured G7 nations into releasing 100 million barrels of oil and diesel from stockpiles to help ease supply concerns, and previously supported calls for a ban on diesel exports from the US.

items.title: NI secretary to ban the Drumcree parade
items.description: The parade has led to a stand-off between Orangemen and nationalist residents of the Garvaghy Road in Portadown lasting almost two weeks.
items.content:
NI secretary to ban the Drumcree parade
- Published
Northern Ireland Secretary Sir Chris Bryant has said he will ban the contentious Orange Order parade at Drumcree.
The dispute has led to a stand-off between Orangemen and nationalist residents of the Garvaghy Road in Portadown lasting almost two weeks.
Sir Chris said the Police Service of Northern Ireland (PSNI) chief constable advised him "that it would not be possible to enable the procession to happen without a major intervention which would carry an unacceptable risk of serious injury, disorder and a wider contagion effect across Northern Ireland".
The move comes on the 13th day of deadlock between residents and the local district lodge of the Orange Order.
The Parades Commission had ruled that the march on Sunday 27 September could go ahead with restrictions in place.
But the parade, from Drumcree Church into Portadown, did not happen due to a large protest on the Garvaghy Road.
Under legislation, a secretary of state can overturn a Parades Commission determination, especially following some form of input from the PSNI.
Sir Chris had been coming under increasing pressure from Sinn Féin and the SDLP to stop the parade.
On Friday night, Sir Chris said: "The Parades Commission have advised me that while ultimately a matter for the courts to determine, the commission is of the view that, in light of this current assessment by the chief constable, the original determination does not now have enduring legal effect.
"Consequently, and in the interests of wider public interest and safety, I've come to the conclusion that the circumstances under which that decision was made have now changed considerably," he said.
"As a result, the procession cannot go ahead as it was determined."
What did the residents say?
Speaking outside a community centre on the Garvaghy Road on Friday night, Garvaghy Road Residents' Coalition spokesman Breandán Mac Cionnaith said that "while this is a win for us tonight, it is one that is still tinged with sadness and with loss".
"There's no real cause for celebration that we have to remember the price that was paid for to get this decision over many years."
Sinn Féin president Mary Lou McDonald said the overwhelming sense on the road was "one of relief and one of joy", adding that this "awful threat and this sense of menace has been lifted from the community".
"To have had the prospect of a march down the road was just incomprehensible, nobody could believe that this decision had been landed and the community said from the get go that they would stand strong and united and that they would not have it and they have. Right has won out here."
Taoiseach (Irish prime minister) Micheál Martin said in a post on social media that the announcement by Sir Chris "will come as a significant relief to the community on the Garvaghy Road".
"It will also be a relief to people in communities right across Northern Ireland, and the island of Ireland as a whole, who were concerned that the situation at Drumcree, if left unresolved, could have had lasting negative repercussions on community relations and reconciliation," he said.
DUP and Orange lodge reaction
The Portadown District said it "notes the chief constable has abdicated his responsibility for policing Northern Ireland".
"We further note that the secretary of state has bowed to the republican mob, and rewarded criminality. Again, the consequences should be self-evident," they said.
The Portadown District said that they "understand the immense anger which is tonight engulfing our community", but has urged for calm.
"The Portadown District will be having no further engagement with the PSNI."
Democratic Unionist Party (DUP) leader Gavin Robinson said in a statement that "it has been clear in recent days that due to the actions of Sinn Féin and the total disregard for the recent determination in favour of a parade that the PSNI cannot ensure the safe completion of the parade".
"The decision of the chief constable to refer the matter to the secretary of state and his conclusion that the parade cannot proceed is a direct result of republican agitation, mobilisation and the looming threats of potential violence," Robinson said.
"These decisions are a mistake, and send profound signals that the country should be run on force of numbers and who shouts the loudest."
What is the Drumcree dispute?
There have been 13 days of deadlock in Portadown since the decision to allow an Orange Order march down the Garvaghy Road on 27 September.
That morning, up to 1,000 people - including politicians such as Northern Ireland First Minister Michelle O'Neill - blocked the road, preventing Orangemen marching from Drumcree Church a mile to the west.
Since then, residents have maintained a constant presence around the road while Orangemen have also repeatedly tried to march the route before being turned back by police.
The Chief Constable, Jon Boutcher, had said last week that the consequences of police forcing an Orange Order march down the Garvaghy Road "could be catastrophic".
He had said while the PSNI's objective was to facilitate the determination, this could not be done "at all costs".
As of last Thursday, the policing operation over the dispute had cost about £3m.
Two weeks ago exactly, the Parades Commission issued a determination saying that the Orange Order parade was to be allowed on the mainly-nationalist Garvaghy Road in Portadown with restrictions in place.
That prompted a legal challenge from the Garvaghy Road Residents' Coalition which opposed the march.
The Court of Appeal is considering whether to allow a challenge to the Parades Commission's ruling, which has been lodged by residents.
Drumcree was one of Northern Ireland's most serious parading disputes, when stand-offs in the mid-to-late 1990s over attempts by the Orange Order to march along the Garvaghy Road were accompanied by riots, roadblocks and killings.
When the Orange Order was prevented by police from walking down the route in July 1995, there was a tense stand-off. It was the same for the next three years.
The Parades Commission began operating in 1998 to regulate parades and try to defuse tension around marches.
Its decision not to allow a march down the Garvaghy Road that summer has been challenged by the order for the past three decades.
Earlier this year the Parades Commission decided that the march could go ahead with restrictions in place after its original decision to stop the march was overturned in court.
Meanwhile, the Court of Appeal is considering its ruling in a legal challenge brought by the residents to block the march going ahead.

items.title: US unveils sanctions on ICC in move court condemns as 'assault on rule of law'
items.description: Several member states of the international tribunal, including the UK, say they "strongly disagree" with the sanctions.
items.content:
US unveils sanctions on ICC in move court condemns as 'assault on rule of law'
- Published
The Trump administration has unveiled sweeping sanctions on the International Criminal Court (ICC) in a significant acceleration of its attempt to "dismantle" what it sees as a "rogue" institution.
US Secretary of State Marco Rubio said the measures - which include a ban on US entities making transactions with the ICC - were intended to "defend US sovereignty" and accused the court of seeking to prosecute Americans.
The ICC said the measures were an assault on the rule of law and the foundations of the international legal order.
The announcement came just hours after former ICC judge Navi Pillay was awarded the 2026 Nobel Peace Prize for her efforts to promote peace and international law.
The US has already sanctioned 17 of the ICC's judges and officials, but this move sanctions the court itself as an institution and is intended to collapse its ability to operate financially.
However, the US has provided a six month grace period before some of these latest sanctions kick in, meaning member states can keep paying for its operations - a move Washington says is to allow countries time to negotiate a "solution to address" US concerns.
UN Secretary General Antonio Guterres called the US decision "a serious blow to our collective pursuit of international criminal justice, of which the ICC is a key pillar".
The UK joined Canada, Denmark, Germany, France, Italy, Japan and the Netherlands in reaffirming their "continued and unwavering support" for the ICC and said they "regret and strongly disagree with" the sanctions.
They also praised the court's staff for their work bringing "those accused of the most serious international crimes to justice", as well as supporting victims.
The ICC was founded in 2002 to prosecute war crimes, crimes against humanity and genocide, and counts 125 countries as member states. Several major countries remain outside the ICC, including the US, Russia, China, India and Israel.
The Trump administration argues the ICC is run by what it calls globalists who threaten American sovereignty.
It is furious over a past investigation into actions of US soldiers in Afghanistan the court has since closed and by its arrest warrants for Israeli officials including Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu. The new sanctions, however, do not say that those warrants must be withdrawn before the measures can be lifted.
But Rubio said Trump would not allow the ICC to prosecute Americans, adding: "Either the ICC will end its threats, or we will end the ICC."
The US sanctions will stop US companies from providing goods or services to the ICC, such as banking or software.
Rubio said Washington had delayed imposing the sanctions in the hope that the ICC and its member countries would address US concerns. He said the measures had been structured to allow other countries to negotiate a possible solution.
He also called on US allies that were ICC signatories, including the UK, to "rein in" the institution.
The Netherlands, which hosts the court in The Hague and is also a Nato ally of the US, faces particular pressure. Dutch Foreign Minister Tom Berendsen has said the sanctions would seriously affect the court's ability to function.
Netanyahu welcomed the sanctions, saying the ICC was "not a court" but a political body that threatened law-abiding democracies and "the very idea of national sovereignty".
The ICC said that the sanctions were aimed at disrupting its work and intimidating those who co-operate with it - but that it "will not be deterred".
It called the measures "an assault on the rule of law" and said no one should be punished for serving the cause of justice, adding: "History will judge this moment."
This showdown potentially marks the gravest crisis in the court's 24-year history. Rather than targeting individual ICC judges and prosecutors, the US is now sanctioning the court itself.
The sanctions could ultimately see the ICC unable to try cases, meaning detainees awaiting trial or judgment could have to be released, according to Professor Ryan Goodman from the New York University School of Law.
Among those awaiting trial in The Hague is Rodrigo Duterte, the former president of the Philippines.
The 81-year-old is accused of the extrajudicial killing of thousands during his deadly "war on drugs" between 2011 and 2019. Others awaiting trial or with pending appeals include former senior figures accused of war crimes in Libya, Sudan and the Central African Republic.
Goodman says that as a senator, Rubio was "out front" highlighting Duterte's alleged crimes.
He told the BBC such a release would be "enormously damaging to the global effort towards international justice [and] towards the Philippines".
"[For] the victims, it just has to be incredibly traumatic because a lot of them participate in the ICC proceedings to put themselves on the line with a hope that justice will come around," adds Goodman, a former special counsel at the US Department of Defence.
Among the carve-outs announced as part of today's sanctions are "licenses" allowing the ICC to continue "services for the operation of facilities used for the detention" of Duterte and others.
However, Goodman says ultimately these detainees may have to be released "as a matter of law" if the financial sanctions mean the court cannot conduct fair trials or appeals.

items.title: Polanski vows to stay on as Green leader as he faces criticism after by-election defeat
items.description: Jewish Greens' leader has said Polanski should resign in the wake of a Zionism row and by-election defeat.
items.content:
Polanski vows to stay as Green leader as he faces criticism after by-election defeat
- Published
Zack Polanski has vowed to stay on as Green Party leader after his by-election defeat, as he faced pressure from within his own party to resign.
The leader of the Jewish Greens, Vivien Lichtenstein, said on Friday he should resign, adding it was a "big mistake" for him to have dodged a debate about a party conference motion that declared Zionism a form of racism.
Lichtenstein's comments come after two former Green leaders accused Polanski of failing to show leadership over the Zionism row.
Polanski, who came second to Labour overnight in the Holborn and St Pancras by-election, told BBC Breakfast he would "absolutely" stay on as leader and he "of course" had not questioned that.
The Greens had hoped to take the seat, previously held by former Prime Minister Sir Keir Starmer, after a by-election success earlier this year.
Polanski lost out in Thursday's contest in London to Labour candidate Sagal Abdi-Wali - who secured 45% of the vote to his 33% - but the Green vote share was up by 22 percentage points on the 2024 general election.
Following the by-election, Lichtenstein was asked whether it would be right for Polanski to continue as leader of the party. She told Times Radio: "No, I think he should resign."
Earlier in the week, Lichtenstein, who has been a member of the Green Party for nearly three decades, told Radio 4's Today programme it was "quite possible" she would leave the party after the Zionism row.
Speaking to the BBC's Victoria Derbyshire on Friday, she said she should would not resign immediately because she is having conversations about how to "detoxify" the party.
When asked if she had confidence in Polanski's leadership, Lichtenstein said: "At the moment, no I don't." She added that she was "very disappointed" in him.
Calling on Polanski to apologise, she said: "I don't think that any Jew in the party is going to be in any danger...
"There just might be some unpleasant people who will direct some unpleasant comments, and some of us are going to have to deal with them robustly."
Her criticisms were similar to those of former Green Party leader Caroline Lucas who said Polanski should have attended the vote on the conference motion on Sunday.
The motion, which was passed by rank-and-file members to become official party policy, defined Zionism as an ideology supporting "an ethnonationalist Jewish state" and backed a "single democratic Palestinian state in all of historic Palestine", which includes modern-day Israel.
Adrian Ramsay, a Green MP and former co-leader, declined to back Polanski on Friday, and said he was now working to reverse the motion.
"A lot depends on what happens in the days and weeks to come," he told the BBC's Politics East, when asked if Polanski should still lead the party.
"[He] did not show leadership I would have been looking for."
'Racist ideology'
Ellie Chowns, the Green MP for North Herefordshire, said she "unequivocally" backs Israel's right to exist and is "passionately opposed to the actions of the current Israeli government under Netanyahu".
"I believe it's for both Israelis and Palestinians themselves to decide what the ultimate constitutional settlement should look like in their region," she told BBC News.
"I believe both Israel and Palestine have the right to exist.
"I believe that's a perspective shared by the large majority of Green Party members and by the large majority of the British people."
Polanski defended his absence from the controversial motion vote in Brighton, saying he was busy campaigning in the North London constituency.
Asked if he would resign, he said: "Of course I can carry on as leader of the Green Party.
"Yes, I've taken a loss tonight but our movement is so much bigger than one election or one motion."
Having not answered questions about the Zionism vote for most of this week, Polanski confirmed in interviews on Friday that he would not have voted for the "imperfect" motion without it being amended.
However, he said "the displacement and genocide of the Palestinian people is clearly underpinned by a racist ideology".
Several UN reports have accused the Israeli government of committing war crimes which amount to genocide in Gaza. Israel has repeatedly denied all such allegations.
On Friday morning, following the Zionism row, Polanski was asked repeatedly on BBC Radio 4's Today programme whether he believes Israel has a right to exist.
"I don't believe any state has the right to oppress or to commit apartheid and certainly not genocide on another people," he said, adding: "I don't believe that's a state that anyone should be supporting."
Asked by presenter Nick Robinson for a "yes/no" answer on this question, he said: "I've repeated many times that I want to see equal rights for Israelis and Palestinians - at the moment Palestinians don't have equal rights so I think I'm answering your question really clearly."
Anger on both sides
In private, plenty of longstanding Green figures remain frustrated and accuse Polanski of being "missing in action" over the motion.
They say the result is an untenable situation where he leads a party whose policy on the Middle East he disagrees with.
"He is in danger of losing the confidence of both wings," one critic pointed out, referring to how some supporters of the motion have now been left irritated too by Polanski's refusal to publicly back them.
- Polanski faces greatest crisis of his leadership so far 
  - Published13 hours ago
- Labour sees off Green challenge to win Holborn by-election 
  - Published9 hours ago
But given his popularity among the grassroots, he may be safe from a leadership challenge in the near future.
Former Green leader Caroline Lucas described the motion as "dangerous" and "flawed from top to bottom", and said leadership "was frankly missing" on it.
She said she was not calling for Polanski to stand down and welcomed that he had "indicated he shares some of my concerns on the Zionism motion".
"Now the party needs to come together to make the urgent changes needed to take us forward," she said.
Jonathan Bartley, the Green co-leader from 2016 to 2021, called on Polanski to "put his hands up" and "say sorry" - but did not demand he quit.
"I think [the vote] was a failure of leadership from Zack and there is a certain toxicity now around the Green Party," he told BBC Radio 4's World at One.
Bartley said the Green brand "needs to be detoxified", adding the party had seen an influx in members that have "maybe come from the left of the Labour Party, maybe from [Jeremy Corbyn's] Your Party" but "we're losing some older voters".
The party's next scheduled leadership ballot takes place in summer 2027, and Bartley said he thinks Polanski will face a challenger.
Siân Berry, Green MP for Brighton Pavilion, said on Friday she was ready to work with colleagues "to restore trust in our processes and our party, fix the serious flaws in the motion that was passed" and build more inclusive policies.
The Green leader has faced days of pressure over the Zionism motion. Four of the five Green MPs and one of the party's two deputy leaders opposed it, the Green deputy in Wales and some councillors resigned, while some local members and the European Green Party have distanced themselves from it.
Prime Minister Andy Burnham has called on Polanski to reverse the "completely wrong" motion.
Meanwhile, Labour chair Bridget Phillipson drew comparisons with her party's previous antisemitism scandal, telling the BBC she felt the Greens now face a "serious problem" with antisemitism.
Polanski has said anti-Zionism and antisemitism are distinct from each other and said nobody will be excluded from the party on the basis of their faith, place of worship or religious body.
- I would not have voted for Zionism motion, Polanski says

items.title: King pays Andrew's £1.5m repair bill on Royal Lodge
items.description: Andrew Mountbatten-Windsor was charged £1.5m in repair and restoration costs after surrendering the lease on the 30-room mansion.
items.content:
King pays Andrew's £1.5m repair bill on Royal Lodge
- Published
King Charles has paid Andrew Mountbatten-Windsor's £1.5m repair bill that's owed for the poor condition of Mountbatten-Windsor's former home at Royal Lodge in Windsor.
It's understood that the money is coming from the King's private income - and will cover what Andrew owes his former landlords, the Crown Estate, on leaving Royal Lodge.
There was a total £1.8m penalty for the "dilapidations" to Royal Lodge, but that has been reduced by the £300,000 Mountbatten-Windsor would have received for an early surrender of his lease.
The Crown Estate say they have not given any money to Mountbatten-Windsor at the conclusion of his lease and have now received the net £1.5m payment they were owed.
- Why did Andrew leave Windsor's Royal Lodge in such a hurry? 
  - Published4 February
- Andrew moves out of Royal Lodge home early after latest Epstein files 
  - Published4 February
Mountbatten-Windsor left his Royal Lodge home in February, in the middle of a storm of revelations about his connections to the US sex offender Jeffrey Epstein.
He has consistently denied any wrongdoing in relation to Epstein.
The former Prince Andrew was moved to Sandringham, with his brother the King using his own money to provide his upkeep and accommodation.
Mountbatten-Windsor was arrested later that month on suspicion of misconduct in public office - and a court ruling on Thursday found fault with the search warrants used by the police.
But despite moving to Sandringham, Mountbatten-Windsor's lease on Royal Lodge had remained until October - and as that officially ends, the Crown Estate is revealing the terms on which it concluded.
When Andrew had taken on the 75 year lease in 2003, he had made considerable up-front payments, including about £7.5m for repairs, which meant that he did not have to pay a monthly rent.
It also meant that if he gave up the lease within the first 25 years he would be legally entitled to some compensation - with that amount reducing each year.
Leaving in October 2026 would have meant that the Crown Estate would have had to pay him back about £302,000.
However that amount has been overshadowed by what he owes to the landlord for the state of the building - and so the Crown Estate says it has now received a net amount of £1.5m.
It's understood that the payment of that money by the King is to avoid leaving the Crown Estate out of pocket.
Whether Mountbatten-Windsor will repay his brother is said to be a private matter - and there are no further details of what this might say about Andrew's personal finances.
There was also no comment on how the King feels about this arrangement - and there is said to be no connection between this payment and the King making clear this week that his financial support should not go to cover Andrew's legal costs in his battle over search warrants.
It has so far not been decided how the 30-room mansion in Windsor will be used in future, but it is expected to be used to deliver a commercial return - and at present there are no plans for another royal occupant.
"The lease for Royal Lodge has ended and our focus now is firmly on its future use and the opportunities to generate additional financial value for the nation from its early return," said a Crown Estate spokesperson.
A report by the National Audit Office had revealed earlier this year that Mountbatten-Windsor had been sub-letting buildings at Royal Lodge, although the amount was never revealed.
That report from the public spending watchdog also showed that Andrew's daughters, Princess Beatrice and Eugenie, had accommodation inside royal palaces which they did not pay for, with the cost being covered privately by the King.

items.title: Trump pleads not guilty to 34 felony counts
items.content:
Watch Trump arrive in New York for his arraignment
1:18
What we covered here
Former President Donald Trump arrived in New York City Monday, a day before he is expected to turn himself in to law enforcement and face more than 30 criminal charges in a Manhattan court following last week’s historic grand jury indictment.
Trump’s legal team said the former president will voluntarily surrender and will look to challenge “every potential issue” once the indictment is unsealed.
Trump, who has vowed to continue his 2024 bid, is the first current or former president in US history who has faced criminal charges. The district attorney’s office has been investigating Trump’s alleged role in a hush money payment scheme involving adult film star Stormy Daniels that dates to the 2016 presidential election.
Trump arraignment has "unparalleled public interest," but it won't be broadcast, judge says
From CNN's Tierney Sneed
Acting New York Supreme Court Judge Juan Merchan wrote his Monday night order that the media’s request to broadcast the arraignment of former President Donald Trump was understandable, but that the news organizations’ interests in providing the broadest possible access to the proceedings must be weighed against “competing interests.”
In rejecting the request to broadcast the arraignment live on television, Merchan still wrote about the historical significance of the proceeding in stark terms.
Link Copied!
Judge will only briefly allow photos in the courtroom before Trump arraignment begins
From CNN's Tierney Sneed
News outlets will not be allowed to broadcast former President Donald Trump’s arraignment on Tuesday in a New York state court, a judge said Monday night, but he will allow some photographers to take pictures in the courtroom before the proceedings formally begin.
Acting New York Supreme Court Judge Juan Merchan rejected the request by several media organizations, including CNN, for permission to broadcast the historic proceedings. Trump’s arraignment — like most arraignments in the Manhattan courthouse — is a public proceeding, but news cameras are not usually allowed to broadcast from inside the courtroom.
However, the judge is allowing five pool photographers to take still photos at the beginning of the proceedings “until such time as they are directed to vacate the jury box by court personnel.”
Earlier on Monday, Trump’s lawyers urged the judge to reject the media’s request for live cameras in the courtroom. The Manhattan District Attorney’s office told the judge they didn’t have a position.
The media outlets that tried to get cameras into the courtroom argued that “the gravity of this proceeding … and, consequently, the need for the broadest possible public access, cannot be overstated.”
The arraignment is also expected to bring the unsealing of the criminal charges against Trump, which have not yet been seen by his lawyers or the public.
The indictment stems from Manhattan District Attorney Alvin Bragg’s investigation into hush-money payments, made during the 2016 presidential campaign, to women who claimed they had extramarital affairs with Trump, which he denies.
Trump denies all wrongdoing and his lawyers said last week that they’ll fight to get the charges dropped.
Link Copied!
Tuesday is the first test for Trump to navigate a legal and political strategy
From CNN's Jeff Zeleny
Donald Trump is not planning to speak publicly in New York on Tuesday, aides say, if he follows advice from members of his legal team who have urged the former President to refrain from the vitriol he’s been directing toward the prosecutor and judge presiding over the case.
But that restraint does not extend to Florida, aides said, where he is planning to deliver a full-throated defense of his New York case as well as other investigations he is facing during a prime time address from Mar-a-Lago on Tuesday night.
It’s the first test to see whether Trump can navigate two vasty different approaches to his legal case and his political campaign, which are now inextricably linked.
Link Copied!
Trump is "ready to go in and do what he needs to do tomorrow," attorney says
From CNN's Mary Kay Mallonee
Alina Habba, lawyer for former President Donald Trump, gives an interview outside of Trump Tower on March 21 in New York City.
(Michael M. Santiago/Getty Images)
Alina Habba, who represents Donald Trump in several civil matters, spent time with the former president in New York today and said, “He’s in good spirits. Honestly, he’s as he normally would be. He’s ready to go in and do what he needs to do tomorrow.”
Habba — appearing on on Fox News’ “Jesse Watters” — was asked about the “game plan” for Trump’s appearance in court in Manhattan Tuesday and said, “It’s all mapped out.”
She added, “Barring any surprises, I think that it should be smooth. We’re trying to coordinate and cooperate with everybody to make sure that there are no problems.”
On whether Trump can get a fair trial in Manhattan, Habba said, “No, no. I think it’s very difficult. I’d like to have faith in this state, but I’ve been practicing for him now for a couple years and gone to court in New York for a few years, and I can tell you, it’s not the same as representing anybody else.”

The former president met with attorneys at Trump Tower on the eve of his arraignment
From CNN's Kristen Holmes
From left to right: Susan Necheles, Todd Blanche and Joe Tacopina.
(Reuters/Getty Images)
Former President Donald Trump met with his attorneys Susan Necheles and Joe Tacopina at Trump Tower after arriving in New York City Monday, a source familiar with the meeting told CNN.
It is unclear if the newest addition to Trump’s New York legal team, Todd Blanche, attended the meeting.
Trump is expected to be arraigned Tuesday.

Photos: Trump arrives in New York City a day before his expected arraignment
From CNN's Photo Desk
Former President Donald Trump has landed in New York’s La Guardia Airport ahead of his expected Tuesday arraignment in a Manhattan courthouse.
History was made Thursday when he was indicted by a New York grand jury. It’s the first time that a current or former US president has been criminally charged.
The Manhattan district attorney’s office has been investigating Trump’s alleged role in a hush money payment scheme and cover-up involving adult film star Stormy Daniels that dates to the 2016 presidential campaign.
Trump’s attorney said he plans to file “substantial” legal challenges. The former president has repeatedly denied wrongdoing in the matter and accused Democrats of targeting him politically.

A supporter of former President Donald Trump holds a "Trump Won" sign outside of Trump Tower in New York on Monday, April 3.
(Alex Kent/Bloomberg/Getty Images)
A small group of supporters chanted as former President Donald Trump arrived at his namesake tower on Monday afternoon, with a handful of people waving banners with messages like “Trump won” and “Arrest Biden.”
While Trump couldn’t see his admirers as he entered a side door on 56th Street, his arrival came with more fanfare and security than at any other time in his post presidency.
Now that he is inside the building — where he launched his presidential bid nearly eight years ago — Trump is expected to meet with lawyers and political advisers on the eve of his arraignment, an aide told CNN.
Trump’s mood was described by an adviser as “defiant and focused,” as he watched expansive television coverage while flying back to his native New York City from Florida.

Special counsel has secured evidence of how Trump handled classified records at Mar-a-Lago, sources say
From CNN's Katelyn Polantz and Evan Perez
Special counsel prosecutors have secured evidence including daily notes, texts, emails and photographs and are focused on cataloging how Donald Trump handled classified records around the Mar-a-Lago resort and those who may have witnessed the former president with them, according to multiple sources familiar with the investigation.
The new details come amid signs the Justice Department is taking steps that are typically near the end of an investigation.
The recent investigative activity before a federal grand jury in Washington, DC, also includes subpoenaing witnesses in March and April who had previously spoken to investigators, the sources said. While the FBI interviewed many aides and workers at Mar-a-Lago nearly a year ago voluntarily, grand jury appearances are transcribed and under oath — an indication the prosecutors are locking in witness testimony.
The focus of both the mishandling of records and obstruction of justice probes has remained on the actions of the former president, the sources say. That includes prosecutors pursuing evidence of Trump’s intent to keep classified records after he left the White House, plus his knowledge that the records remained in his possession after the Justice Department demanded their return last May.
Witnesses are being questioned about what they saw in Trump’s private residential and work areas within the club, some of the sources said.
